text:
Alexandre Texier has been one of the quiet good things about Montreal's start, even if the scoresheet hasn't noticed. With him on the ice at five on five, the Canadiens have held 57% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality), about nine points better than when he sits. He's getting looks of his own too: 2 goals on 4.2 expected.

The finish is what's missing. He's shooting 5.7% against a talent range of roughly 10 to 14%, and he's gone pointless in seven straight games on 2.7 expected points. Our numbers read that as a player who is due, not one who has dried up, and his ice time has crept up to 14.3 minutes over the last ten games.

He also carries a real shot: his hardest this season, 89.4 mph, sits in the 88th percentile.

The thing to watch now is availability. He missed Tuesday's practice, as RotoWire and Dose.ca reported, with no reason given in the reports we have. If he's back, the chances suggest the points follow.
